To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a novel DNA regulatory sequence, the septamer, is present in the promoter regions of genes expressed in neuronal and glial lineages and that the DNA sequence is bound by three lineage-specific protein complexes that are assembled from distinct nuclear proteins.

(1) the DNA regulatory element, termed the septamer, is present on a number of genes that are differentially activated by progenitors as they differentiate into neurons and glial; (2) the DNA regulatory elements serve as binding site for a family of proteins, termed septamer binding proteins (SBP), which are expressed in a lineage-specific manner; (3) the binding of the SBPs to the septamer causes a DNA bending which may contribute to their lineage-specific regulatory effect;

“A novel DNA element (TTT GCAT = septamer), present on a number of neuron- and astrocyte-specific genes, binds to three distinct protein complexes, which cause a lineage-specific DNA bend and may regulate neuroglial development.”
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that control the development of neurons and glia from progenitor cells.
the mechanisms of neuronal and glial differentiation in the CNS.
the molecular mechanisms that control the development of the mammalian nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the septamer DNA regulatory element and its binding proteins are novel protein-DNA interactions that may contribute significantly to the regulation of neural cell differentiation in developing mammalian CNS.

the septamer element is a DNA regulatory element present on a number of neuron- and astrocyte-specific genes and that the binding proteins (p-sept, n-sept and g-sept) are lineage-specific transcription factors that may play a role in the differentiation of neuronal and astrocytic lineages.
septamer element-binding proteins in neuronal and glial differentiation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the septamer element is a novel DNA element that is involved in the regulation of neuro-glial differentiation.
we have identified a novel regulatory DNA sequence (TTTGC AT = Septamer) that regulates neuronal and glial differentiation.
septamer and its associated proteins represent a novel DNA regulatory system for the regulation of neuronal and glial differentiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a novel DNA element (septamer) present in many neuronal and glial genes is bound by a family of proteins, and these interactions may be important for neuronal and glial differentiation in the CNS.
a DNA sequence (TTTGCATAA) is present in the promoter regions of many neuronal and glial genes.
the DNA regulatory elements and the protein complexes that bind to them are not static, but change as the cell lineage progresses.
